blocks.text: Real-world analogue: Cappadocian cave settlements, desert refuges hidden by landform, forest blinds, animal burrows with several escape routes, old cities with nested courtyards, and buildings whose public façade conceals a much deeper interior.

World relation: Quiet Worlds contribute concealment and controlled observation. Continuity Worlds contribute protected memory. Open World values appear only in carefully chosen common rooms and Bridges.

Connection to newer locations: Shelter logic survives in the Redwood Rain Vault, Urban Canyon Hive, Karst Lantern Provinces, Mangrove Cathedral, and Still-Loading Forest. Each protects life by regulating how it can be found.
Abstract or metaphorical relation: Privacy is not absence. The Veil is a boundary that permits relationship without surrendering every interior to inspection.
